text:
maria: seeing p95 east-west latency spikes between GPU nodes during our 10:00-11:00 batch window. started ~10:30 UTC. infer-cluster-3, batch jobs 6-9. NIC counters show rx drops on eno2 and some retransmits.

dave: are these RDMA flows or normal TCP? any obvious topology change?

maria: mostly RDMA (ibverbs) for model KV cache and TCP for control. tcpdump on one affected pod shows retransmits and dup acks around the same time as the p95 jump.

raj: checked ToR counters briefly — ECMP path distribution looks lopsided for the 5-tuple hash. some spillover to a 2:1 link, others underutilized. also qdisc backlog drop spikes on hosts. fq_codel shows drops aligned to the window.

olivia: deploy-bot alerted earlier: "Alert: eastwest-latency-p95 > 60ms for infer-cluster-3". any quick mitigations? :alarm_clock:

maria: pasted small snippet from ethtool -S on node-gpu-12 showing the noisy counters:

```
ethtool -S eno2
rx_packets: 18234567
rx_errors: 0
rx_dropped: 428
rx_crc_errors: 0
tx_packets: 17233421
tx_dropped: 12
rdma_rx_queue_drops: 312
```

(drops aren't huge but correlate tightly with the batch spikes)

dave: what NICs/driver/firmware? mlx5? kernel bump recently?

maria: mlx5, firmware on these hosts is 43.31.0, we did a kernel update from 5.15 -> 5.19 on 40% of fleet last week (canary). affected hosts are mixed.

raj: I pulled softirq/steal metrics — node-gpu-12 shows big softirq spikes during window, likely NAPI/irq steering falling back. irqstat snippet:

```
all  120000
CPU0 90000 softirq
```

If NIC can't keep up with steering, packets hit process path and latency jumps.

dave: that plus ECMP imbalance smells like both NIC steering + switch hashing interaction after the kernel bump (RSS behavior changed). Could be that Mellanox driver change altered steering masks.

olivia: MTU status? we've had PMTU issues before causing reassembly cost.

maria: MTU is 9000 on hosts, but a subset of ToRs still on 1500 due to a config drift we partially fixed last quarter. I saw signs of fragmentation on a few flows earlier in packet captures.

raj: fragmentation + fq_codel drops + ECMP hotspot = microbursts that show as p95 spikes during batching ramp.

dave: short-term mitigation plan I propose:
- disable fq_codel on eno2 on 10% of affected hosts as a canary (switch to pfifo_fast) during next window\- pin RDMA flows with RROCE path policy to avoid the 2:1 oversubscribed ECMP path\- ask network team to re-evaluate ECMP hash config (use src/dst port+ip)

maria: +1 on canary. I can flip qdisc and run a controlled batch to compare. will collect tcpdump + perf counters.

olivia: I'll open a network ticket to check ToR CPU and ECMP config, and request a firmware review for the mlx5 devices. setting DSCP for RDMA might help prioritization too.

deploy-bot: action created: #INFRA-2043 "investigate east-west p95 spikes infer-cluster-3" assigned to raj, dave, maria, olivia. due: 48h.

raj: longer term: consider aligning kernel/driver across fleet before batch windows (rolling windows) and add a small leaky bucket queue at the host egress to smooth bursts from batched requests. also evaluate prefix KV cache to cut inter-node chatter by ~30%.

maria: I'll attach pcaps and ethtool + irqstat dumps after next run. for now enabling request coalescing in the router seems a low-risk win.

olivia: thanks — if the canary shows improvement we'll schedule a fleet-wide qdisc change and coordinate a firmware roll. :thumbsup:

maria: collecting artifacts now, will post within 30m.
